items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: erms with Nat Towles -- those kind of bands out in the southwest, and they'd been traveling for years.

ctx.x: Skeets Washley was his name. He was out of Hannibal, Missouri. And Flip -- and Charles, our alto player, was out of Texas; his drummer was out of Kansas City, George Smith; Mitch Franklin was out from the southwest somewhere out there; he's still living, and Flip -- now, I can't remember exactly where Flip was from -- but they all come out of that Blue Devil's Band, you see; they worked -- and Flip told me he had worked with Walter Page Blue Devil's big band man, and they were on good
terms with Nat Towles -- those kind of bands out in the southwest, and they'd been traveling for years. You know, before I joined them.
Like I said, this was an education for me.
